summary: Add a new nullable column `customer_note`, keep it in sync with the existing `note` column via triggers, backfill existing data, deploy the new code, then drop the old column after the old version is retired.
write_consistency: During the overlap both Django versions write to different columns. Two BEFORE triggers keep `note` and `customer_note` identical on every INSERT/UPDATE, so reads from either version always see the latest value and no data is lost.

stages.description: Add the new column and create triggers that mirror changes between `note` and `customer_note`.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note text;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_note_to_customer_note BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF note ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer_note();
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_customer_note_to_note BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF customer_note ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_customer_note_to_note();

stages.description: Copy existing values from `note` to `customer_note` in batches until all rows are synchronized.
sql: WITH batch AS (SELECT id FROM account_user WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND (customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM note) LIMIT 1000) UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note FROM batch WHERE account_user.id = batch.id;

stages.description: Deploy the new Saleor version that uses the `customer_note` field.
Remove synchronization triggers and drop the obsolete `note` column after the old version is retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;

stages.description: Retire the old application version; only the new version remains.
